items.q: China already has 130,000 km of inland waterway. What was missing?
items.a: Draft. Only the **Yangtze** and the **Pearl** could take a stable **5,000-ton** ship. Pinglu (16 Sept 2026) is the **third trunk**, 134.2 km, mid-Pearl to Qinzhou.
The Yangtze moves **80%+** of inland freight. Three Gorges peak wait: **200+ hours**. Pearl busiest hub: **100+**. The cut is a queue dump, not a postcard.

sections.title: The dirt has to go somewhere

items.q: What do you do with a ridge between two rivers 10 km apart?
items.a: Move it. **315 million m³** (~120 Great Pyramids). Bigger than any current domestic transport job. Tianjin Hao shows up in the cut.

items.q: Did the canal eat the fields?
items.a: [[spoil-as-new-plain]]. ~9% into fill and pits. The rest lifts ravines. Net arable **+835.7 ha**. Cane, then drones and wind on the same dirt.

items.q: Why not just let the river run?
items.a: 65 m drop in 134 km. ~5× lower Pearl, ~10× Grand Canal. Three two-way hubs: 马道, 企石, 青年. Chamber **300 × 34 × 40 m**.
[[water-saving-lock-stack]]. One dump ≥**300,000 tons**. Only **1.8%** of headwater is spare. Stacked pools ~60%; twin locks ~50%. **16 minutes** fill/empty.
[[inland-not-geographic-destiny]]. 560 km shorter. **¥5B+**/year. ~two weeks off a Southwest Yangtze haul. 50M Guangxi, 250M Southwest. 湘桂 is named as the next stitch.

items.q: Who is the silent watcher at Qinzhou?
items.a: Sun Yat-sen. 建国方略, ~100 years early. The statue is the rhyme. The file is the locks.
